Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:6: And He emanated five worlds, one the soul of the next and so on down: they are Adam Kadmon (the Primordial Man), mentioned in Sefer HaTikkunim (in Tikkun 19, at the beginning of Tikkun 70, and in several places), and called by the early sages Tzachtzachot; the second is the World of Atzilut (Emanation); the third, the World of Beriah (Creation); the fourth, the World of Yetzirah (Formation); the fifth, the World of Assiyah (Action). And these five worlds are called one Havayah (the Name), for the tip of the yud is Adam Kadmon, the yud itself is Atzilut, the first heh is Beriah, the vav is Yetzirah, and the final heh is Assiyah.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:7: And since Adam Kadmon, due to its extreme concealment, has no image of a letter at all except for the tip of the yud — for the Infinite has no image even of a tip — therefore we never mention more than four worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah, for these are complete letters, and all four together are called the Name Havayah:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:8: Furthermore, these four are divided into nine levels: Chochmah and Binah and the six extremities (Tiferet) and Malchut. For these four are called the four supernal elements, which are the four worlds Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah, and they are divided into ten sefirot. And indeed the tip of the yud, which is Adam Kadmon, the fifth, supernal world, includes them all, and within it alone is the root of all four elements, which are the four worlds Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah, Assiyah; and it follows that there are never more than four elements. The sum of the matter is that the Ein Sof is not included in any reckoning whatsoever:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:9: And afterward come the worlds. At first they are one totality, one Name of Havayah, and afterward it divides into four elements, apart from their root, which is Adam Kadmon, the tip of the yud, which is the tenth sefirah, the highest of all, called Keter (Crown); and afterward these four elements divide into ten sefirot, as mentioned:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:10: And all this is included in two categories: the Emanator and all the emanated. And this is what is written in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (ch. 23): before the world was created — meaning this world — He and His Name were one, for the Ein Sof, called "He," and the emanated beings included within His Name, which is one Havayah, are all one, for the flame was hidden within the coal:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:11: Now it has been explained that all the worlds are included in the Name Havayah, which divides into four elements and ten sefirot, and likewise each individual world is detailed in this same manner. How so? Behold, the World of Atzilut, which is the letter yud, called Chochmah, is divided into all the aspects mentioned, and within it is one complete Havayah, divided into four elements and ten complete sefirot, in the same manner mentioned regarding the totality of all the worlds, exactly; and this is so in every one of the five worlds mentioned, and in this way the matter continues to be detailed in the utmost particularity, until it is found that even in this lowly world, there is no creature so lowly that it does not contain the totality of the four letters of Havayah and the totality of the ten sefirot. And all this is to show that everything is created by the power of the Emanator, blessed be He, and there is nothing besides Him:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:12: There is yet another preliminary principle: all these aspects and levels, from the height of Adam Kadmon down to the depths of this lowly world, are each above the other and each within the other, for the one higher than its fellow clothes itself within the one lower than it, like a soul within a body. However, not the entire totality of the higher one clothes itself in the lower one, but only a particular, lowest aspect of the higher one clothes itself in the entire lower one, and so it continues in this manner until the end of the worlds. Thus, all the worlds — whether in their totality or in any particular aspect of them, even in the lowly world, in every detail of it — are all this way: this one is higher than that one, and this one more inward than that one, until all of them are, as it were, garments one to another, and all of them are garments to the Ein Sof, the soul of all souls:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:13: Now, in each of these five worlds there is a difference in the extension of the lights, as to how far they reach, so that there be a distinction between one and another; and there is likewise another distinction within the particulars of the four elements in each world, and likewise within the particulars of the particulars, and this is not the place to elaborate on this matter:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:14: And it is found that just as, in the manner of the extension of the lights from above to below, there is no sefirah that is not included of all ten sefirot, and every sefirah divides into thousands and myriads of sefirot, so is the matter in the extension of the lights from within to without: the innermost of all is called Keter, and the one outer to it is Chochmah, and the one outer to it is Binah, and the one outer to it is the six extremities of Tiferet, and the outermost of all is Malchut; and likewise every single aspect divides in this manner into thousands and myriads of particular details.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:15: And since the explanation of this matter has already been given by us regarding all the other worlds except the matter of Assiyah, we shall therefore explain its matter here in the utmost brevity, insofar as is needed for the discourse we seek here:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:16: Behold, there are seven firmaments, and the highest is called Aravot, since it includes the first three sefirot of Assiyah, namely: the sphere of the intellect, the sphere that encompasses, the sphere of the constellations; and five spheres — Shabtai (Saturn), Tzedek (Jupiter), Ma'adim (Mars), Chamah (the Sun), Nogah (Venus) — which are Chesed, Gevurah, Tiferet, Netzach, Hod; and a sixth sphere, Yesod, includes Kochav (Mercury) and Levanah (the Moon).
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:17: And the last one is called Vilon, and has no function at all (Chagigah 12b), for it is the sefirah of Malchut of Assiyah, and it too divides into ten sefirot within itself. They are: Vilon, its Keter; and the four elements — fire, air, water, earth — of this lowly world, which are Chochmah and Binah and the six extremities of Tiferet and Malchut. And it is found that the Malchut within its own Malchut is the element of earth, the vessel and raw material for the entire world, and within this element of earth are found all its offspring, composed of all four elements mentioned, in the mystery of "all was from the dust":
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:18: And this has been explained from above to below, and likewise it is so from within to without. For behold, the element of earth is composed of ten sefirot, and the Keter within them is the innermost of all, called the aspect of yechidah of the element of earth. And outer to it, Chochmah. And outer to it, Binah, [called] neshamah. And outer to it, the six extremities of Tiferet, [called] ruach. And outer to it, Malchut, [called] nefesh of the element of earth. And this Malchut divides into ten sefirot within itself, and the outermost Malchut among them is the element of earth itself, material, which has no spirituality at all but is turbid matter, called domem (mineral/inanimate), and everything within it is called the nefesh of the domem.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:19: And likewise regarding the element of water, for the outermost Malchut among them all is called the growing waters and is called tzomeach (vegetative), and everything within it is called the nefesh of the tzomeach. And likewise regarding the element of air, and the element of fire, which are chai (animate) and medaber (speaking). And indeed, all four together are: the domem — nefesh; and the tzomeach — ruach; and the chai — neshamah; and the medaber — chayah; and the Vilon — yechidah. And we have already explained that each aspect of these is included of all of them.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:20: And this is what you find in the words of the philosophers, spoken of as "faculties" — that in the vegetative soul there is the nourishing faculty, the attracting faculty, the digesting faculty, and the expelling faculty; and likewise they said regarding the animal soul, called the motive and sensory [soul], that within it there is the arousing faculty, the imaginative faculty, and the depicting faculty, and so on for all of them in this manner.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 1:21: The upshot of all this is that even though the outermost Malchut of any given aspect is the "body" of that aspect, it is nonetheless not called a true, turbid body or matter, except for the outermost, final Malchut of Assiyah, from above to below and from within to without — this point alone is the element of earth, wholly material, and it is the most turbid and material "body" of all the worlds together:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:1-4: On the nature of man — and in it we shall explain discourses that the earlier ones did not fathom, and these are wondrous foundations, and were it not necessary to explain matters of prophecy I would not have explained them, and I shall write them in the utmost brevity, "lambs for your clothing."
And I shall ask several profound questions:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:5: 1. What need was there for the creation of man in this world with a body and a soul?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:6: 2. Why did He further add, in the formation of man, two further formations, namely the good inclination and the evil inclination within him?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:7: 3. Since both of them are equally balanced within him, how was free choice given to tip him toward one or the other, and by what power? And if there is the ability to tip [the balance], then they should not be created at all.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:8: 4. An explanation of these two inclinations — what is their nature?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:9: 5. To know whether the soul of man is greater than the angels or not. If we say that man is greater than the angels, why did the angels not also come down into this world to clothe themselves in a body and a soul? And if the angel is greater than man, this is impossible, for in all the midrashim of our Sages, of blessed memory, we find the opposite, as they said (Midrash Rabbah, Vayishlach ch. 78), which is greater, the guardian or the guarded, and the like. Moreover, the verses themselves indicate the opposite, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:18), "You neglected the Rock who bore you," (Psalms 68:35) "ascribe strength to God, His majesty is over Israel," (Deuteronomy 14:1) "you are children to the Lord your God," (Isaiah 49:3) "Israel, in whom I shall be glorified." And the angels do not say "Kadosh" until Israel begins; nothing like this is found regarding the angels at all.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:10: 6. And even if we admit that this is so, it is a great wonder to call them "children" and to say that they weaken the supernal power, or strengthen it, or that He glories in them, as it were — and a person might thereby come to heresy.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:11: 7. The matter of prophecy — how is it possible that the King of kings should speak, even through an angel, to lowly man, and how much more so while he is clothed in the most turbid matter of all the worlds?
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:12: Now, it has already been explained in the gate preceding this one, regarding the nature of the worlds, how they are all one Havayah that includes them all and divides into five worlds, which are called yechidah, chayah, neshamah, ruach, and nefesh. And this material world is the body and matter for them all. Thus all the worlds are the forms of Adam (man), composed of matter and form, dividing into five kinds of spirituality, as mentioned. And you know that the Name Havayah spelled out in full with alephs equals, by gematria, Adam (man). And in this manner it is so with every particular, in all its aspects, and each aspect of them is called a particular Adam, comprised of one Havayah divided into four elements and ten sefirot:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:13: There is yet another distinction not explained in the preceding gate, namely that the ten sefirot themselves divide into 613 aspects, as will be explained. And behold, all the worlds together, and likewise each particular one of them by itself, was created in the likeness of the lower man, and this is the mystery of "let us make man in our image, according to our likeness" — understand this well:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:14: And it has already been explained (Etz Chaim, Gate 47, ch. 7) that from Beriah downward, all is called the Tree of Knowledge, composed of good and evil, but at each level the good diminishes and the evil increases, until it is found that the lowly world is mostly evil and only a little good. It has also been explained that in this world, evil always crowns the tzaddik (righteous one), and therefore the good is called the "fruit" and the evil is called the kelipah (peel/shell) that clothes the fruit — and not only this, but even the good lights themselves are in this manner, for the purest and most spiritual among them clothes itself within the rest of the lights, and so all of them, according to the order of their levels. And it has already been explained in the preceding gate how the Ein Sof is innermost of all, and outer to it the sefirot in the order of their levels, Keter innermost of all and Malchut outermost of all:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:15: And now let us explain what was not explained there. It is that just as this particular light, called the world of the ten sefirot, is in the shape of one Adam, so too there is another light called the quarry of the souls of human beings, included exactly within all those particular aspects explained regarding the Adam of the ten sefirot, which is called complete divinity, and it clothes itself within this light called the quarry of the souls, in all its particulars:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:16: There is yet another light, in the form of Adam, called the quarry of the angels, from which all the angels were hewn, and it too is included of all the aforementioned particulars, and it is an outer garment over the light of the quarry of the souls:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:17: And there is yet another, smaller light, called a dark light, and it is entirely harsh judgments, from which all the kelipot of that world were emanated, and it clothes itself over the light of the quarry of the angels, and it too is in the shape of Adam. And outer to all the lights mentioned are the very firmaments of that world, and they are called the "body" of that world; and within it are the five lights mentioned: the light of the Ein Sof, according to the level of that world, is innermost of all; and upon it, the light of the ten sefirot; and upon it, the light of the quarry of the souls; and upon it, the light of the quarry of the angels; and upon it, the light of the quarry of the kelipot; and upon it, the world itself, which is the firmaments, the "body" of the lights mentioned. And afterward, within this body called the firmaments, the offspring of that world were created, and they are composed of all these aspects, for each one of them has a force drawn from the firmaments, which is its "body," and within it the light of judgments, and within it the light of the angels, and within it the light of the quarry of the souls, and within it the light of the ten sefirot, riding upon them all and giving them life:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:18: And that force drawn from the light of the quarry of the souls is called the supernal fortune (mazal) of the soul of the lowly man — understand this well. Except that in Beriah it is called the fortune of the neshamah, and in Yetzirah it is called the fortune of the ruach, and in Assiyah it is called the fortune of the nefesh:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:19: And now let us explain the nature of man, what its matter is. Let us begin his existence from the World of Assiyah, from Malchut and upward,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:20: It has already been explained what each world is, and also what the offspring of that world are. Now the World of Assiyah first has the lowest portion mentioned, its Malchut, called the four elements of the lowly world, and all its offspring were created in its "body," which is in the material element of earth, and they divide into four categories,
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:21: The lowest of them, precious stones and metals, which contain only the element of earth, which received power from all four elements together, from their "body," and these were mixed together and became that metal; but within it there is a single force that mixed together this admixture, and it is called the nefesh of the element of earth, comprising its five aforementioned faculties:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:22: Afterward the vegetative was created, such as trees and grasses, whose body was of the element of earth, and so on, and it has the nefesh of the domem befitting it, and added to it the nefesh of the vegetative, composed of its five faculties:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:23: Afterward the chai (living, animal) was created, namely beasts and birds and so on, and they have a body and the nefesh of the domem and the nefesh of the vegetative, with the nefesh of the chai added to them, called the animal soul, [which possesses] movement and sensation:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:24: Afterward the speaking man was created, and he has all the aforementioned faculties, with the speaking soul from the element of fire added to them:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:25: But know that certainly all the aspects of body and forms within man are more refined than those of the chai, and those of the chai more than those of the tzomeach, and those of the tzomeach more than those of the domem, and this will be explained to you from what I wrote above: that each aspect of them is included of all of them, in the order of one within the other:
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:26: And afterward He created the Israelite man, more refined in all his aspects than all the other creatures, in his body and in the four aspects of his souls — the domem, the tzomeach, the chai, and the medaber — from the innermost, purest part of each of the four elements they are composed of and in their form, meaning the souls within them.
Sha'arei Kedusha, Part 3 2:27: And because he is more refined than all the creatures on earth, he was further elevated, in that he too is included and bound up with all the worlds and all their particulars, from below to above. How so? First a nefesh from the firmament of Vilon enters him, and from there upward until the highest firmament of Assiyah, all of which is called the nefesh of Assiyah, and this is called the holy intellective soul (nefesh sichlit) within man. And this itself divides into five faculties, yechidah, chayah, and so on:
